title: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions
author: Arthur Bennett (Editor, Compiler)
edition_analyzed: Banner of Truth Trust standard edition
target_audience: Christians seeking to deepen personal devotion and prayer life
Those interested in Puritan theology and spirituality
core_themes: Confession of sin and assurance of grace
Reverence and awe toward God's holiness
Petition for guidance and spiritual growth
Struggles and assurance in the Christian journey
primary_purpose: To provide believers with a rich treasury of Puritan prayers and meditations, fostering a deeper, more thoughtful, and theologically grounded devotional life rooted in humility, repentance, and faith.

structure_format.organization: Arranged topically into sections (e.g., Father, Son, Ministry, Penitence) and composed of individual prayers/meditations rather than chapters
features: Theological language reflective of Puritan tradition
No references to specific scripture passages within prayers
Preface by the compiler explaining the purpose and approach

key_concepts_lessons: True spirituality is marked by humility and constant dependence on God's grace.
Prayer encompasses adoration, confession, thanksgiving, and supplication.
Repentance and the acknowledgment of personal need are central to spiritual health.
Christ's work is the foundation for all hope and assurance.
Heartfelt devotion is enhanced by rich, thoughtful language and meditation.
Puritan prayers often focus on the majesty of God, sinfulness of the human heart, and the sufficiency of Christ.
notable_features: Unique compilation of prayers from various 17th-18th century Puritan writers
Emphasis on written, structured prayer as aid to devotion
Rich, formal, and expressive English style
Widely used in modern Christian devotion despite its historical language and sources
cultural_historical_context: Originally composed from the writings of English and American Puritans (16th-18th centuries), the 1975 compilation brought their devotional style to a new generation, responding to modern believers' desire for deep, heart-searching prayer in contrast to contemporary, informal trends.
reception_impact: Highly regarded among evangelicals, Reformed Christians, and those interested in spiritual classics
Frequently recommended as a daily devotional resource
Praised for spiritual depth and language, though some find the style archaic or challenging
Sparked renewed interest in Puritan spirituality and literature
comparable_titles: Piercing Heaven: Prayers of the Puritans (Robert Elmer, ed.)
The Puritans: Their Origins and Successors by Martyn Lloyd-Jones
Prayers of the Early Church by J. Manning Potts (ed.)
